children.innerHTML: Fathom is a small school anchored over a 42-metre blue hole. We teach people to dive it on a single breath, calmly, in their own time.
The sea still argues for the surface here. Equalise early, equalise often, spend nothing.
Heart rate down by a quarter. The body remembers it was born for this.
The water stops pushing you up. For one weightless moment, nobody is winning.
Stop kicking. Fold in. Let the blue do the last of the work.
Bottom of the line. Take the tag, turn, and want the light more than you fear the dark.

Everyone dives the same line.
Nobody dives the same dive.
of house line, checked every morning, dived every day
divers per coach, never more, whatever the season
gadgets between you and the water. One breath is the whole kit
Breathwork on the beach, statics in the shallows, your first quiet metres on the line.
Equalisation that finally clicks, free immersion, constant weight, and a 20-metre exam dive.
Mouthfill, real freefall, and one unhurried dive to the bottom of the house line.
“The sea is the last quiet room on earth. Nobody can reach you down there, including your own excuses.”
